checks.claim: Section 2 local norm (8) and its derivation
checks.reason: Fixed-mask (6) and (6a) give sup and seminorm bounds that combine to N_ell(I_D V)<=2max(1,C_theta)[D]_theta ell^theta N_ell(V). Right multiplication by V(r) has operator norm at most ||V(r)|| on B(F), so the (4.3) application is dimension free.

checks.claim: Small-d case: log sup||U_D||<=2c_theta B^theta d
checks.reason: Contraction at ell=B with u=c_theta d B^theta<=1/4 gives N_B(U)<=1/(1-u). The inequality -log(1-u)<=2u holds on [0,1/4]. There is zero cost at d=0 and no prefactor.

checks.claim: Large-d piece count and refined bound (9)
checks.reason: u>1/4 is equivalent to x=B(4c_theta d)^nu>1, using theta nu=1, so n_D=ceil(x)<=2x. Then ell^theta<=1/(4c_theta d), which gives ratio at most 1/4. Each piece contributes a factor at most 4/3, so log sup<=n_D log(4/3)<=C d^nu. Combining with the small-d case gives exp(c(d+d^nu)) with no per-block prefactor.

checks.claim: Uniform inverse and Holder bounds (10), including partition boundaries
checks.reason: Each piece has N_ell(Q)<=4/3 and sup||Q-I||<=1/3, so the Neumann series gives sup||Q^-1||<=3/2. Dividing (8) by ell^theta gives a local seminorm of order K times the initial norm. Pairs at distance below ell cross at most one boundary of the uniform partition and are handled by concavity with factor 2^(1-theta). Larger distances use 2sup||U||/ell^theta. The inverse identity U^-1(t)-U^-1(s)=-U^-1(t)(U(t)-U(s))U^-1(s) was re-derived and is correct. No dimension enters.

checks.claim: Trilinear Young integral G(s)(Z)=R Z U with Ctheta bound (11)
checks.reason: G takes values in B(B(F)). The bounds sup||G||<=sup||R||sup||U|| and [G]_theta<=[R]sup||U||+sup||R||[U] are correct. Primary (4.3) with V=W=B(F) gives Z_(s,t)=G(s)X_(s,t)+O(|t-s|^(2theta)). Since Z(0)=0, ||Z||theta<=L'x. No tensor or commutation assumption is used.

checks.claim: Full 2theta increment expansion and factorization (12)-(13) with LEFT order
checks.reason: P_(s,t)=U_(s,t)V(s)+U(s)V_(s,t)+U_(s,t)V_(s,t). The cross term is O(2theta). Substitution with U(s)R(s)=I gives (H+X)_(s,t)P(s)+O(2theta). The remainder sum is at most B mesh^(2theta-1), which tends to 0 on arbitrary partitions. P is in Ctheta, so left-point sums converge to the Young integral, and uniqueness in the Ctheta class gives U_(H+X)=U_H V. The side formula dR=-R dH was also checked. The smooth-matrix control confirms the same order.

checks.claim: E1 conclusion, including arbitrary bounded A and the physical endpoint
checks.reason: A U_(H+X)(t)=A U_H(t) V(t) with ||V||<=exp(C(x+x^nu)) follows from (9) and (11), which gives (1) for all bounded A, including A=0 and noninvertible A. No invertibility of A is used, no smooth density in full Holder norm is asserted, and the exact factor ||A U_H(t)|| is retained.

checks.claim: E2 mean path: C3 primitive without sqrt(delta), delta-Lr budget, true last block
checks.reason: C3 (13) is a bound on the primitive of an arbitrary Lr(I;K(F)) field and applies directly to M=T Phi. That gives ||H_m||theta<=a_m, with the constant C_B unchanged for ell_m<=B and for ell_m=0. The change of variables gives delta sum a_m^r=C_B^r||T Phi||Lr(I)^r<=D_M.

checks.claim: Actual GIVEN-W head identity (5), raw coefficient sqrt(delta), tuple a.s. identity, D1(8) fit
checks.reason: Transfer is linear on jointly Gaussian noises W(P_J T f) and W(Q_J T f), and the bounded F extension and stopping preserve this. C3 (12) at rank 0 gives E[g_delta A_m W(e_j)]=sqrt(delta)H_m(e_j). Since E[X_m W(e_j)]=0, the head equals H_m(Phi_delta,J) by pathwise linearity of H_m. Independent first-chaos check: ell(X^0-X^J)=W(P_J k_ell)=sum_j ell(L^0 e_j)W(e_j), which agrees with D1(8). Countable statistics and finitely many m give one event per fixed delta,J. No uniformity over delta is claimed.

checks.claim: Closed-range constant-coordinate baseline ||P_m^0||>=1, not relying on E dense in F
checks.reason: T Phi(s) has range in closed iE and S_F preserves iE, so pi_C H_m=0 by bounded functional action on Bochner integrals. Riemann sums give pi_C U=pi_C, and pi_C S_F(t)=tau(t)pi_C. The input (0,1,0) has norm 1 and output constant coordinate tau(ell)(1,0)=(1,0), so the norm is at least 1. This includes ell_m=0. No density of E in F is used.

checks.claim: Good/bad comparison (16)-(17) and first assertion of (4), with c_B independent of K,J,delta,Phi,M and C_K absorbing the residual coefficient
checks.reason: Good blocks use E1 with A=S_F(ell_m). Bad blocks use (9) on a_m+v_m together with y<=1+y^nu and convexity, so c_B depends only on theta,B,G_B. The baseline is at least 1, so log||P_m^0||>=0 and division cannot raise the bound. C_K=max(c_B, good constant) absorbs c_B v^nu. log max(1,z)<=RHS holds because RHS>=0.

checks.claim: Second assertion of (4): exponent signs on exceptional blocks
checks.reason: For a>K>=1 and r>nu: (a/K)^r>=1 and a^(nu-r)<=K^(nu-r) since nu-r<0. Summing with (14) gives D_M(K^-r+K^(nu-r)).

checks.claim: Finite Holder (18) and the existing Mathlib type application
checks.reason: The packet type is (sum f)^p<=card^(p-1) sum f^p, with hypotheses 1<=p and nonnegative f on s. With kappa=p/nu>=1 and f=v^nu>=0, (v^nu)^(p/nu)=v^p holds for v>=0 including zero bases. Raising to nu/p>0 and multiplying by delta gives (delta n)^(1-nu/p)Y^nu. nu=p gives kappa=1 and equality. n=N+1>=2. No new kernel, theorem or count is claimed.

checks.claim: Section 6 joint continuity and Borel measurability, with sup outside expectation and finite expectations uniform in Phi
checks.reason: Phi->H_m is bounded linear into B0 at fixed delta. The fixed-mask Young map is locally Lipschitz on bounded balls, and the denominators are at least 1 for every Phi. Separability of H and B0^n gives product-Borel joint measurability, Tonelli gives a Borel expectation, and no random supremum appears. Finiteness comes from D1(3).

checks.claim: Slack inequality and (19), including eta formula and independence of J,delta
checks.reason: v<=tau+tau^(1-nu)v^nu holds in both cases. delta n<=1/B+delta<2/B and 1-nu/p>=0. Expanding q log max(1,z)<=q c_B S_bad+q C_K[n tau+(1+tau^(1-nu))sum v^nu] gives (19) exactly, with eta=q C_K(1+tau^(1-nu))(2/B)^(1-nu/p). eta contains no J or delta. The D1 finite replacement bound matches D1(3) with s=C0 epsilon_J.

checks.claim: Iterated limit (20) and (6): order delta, J, tau, K, with a genuine ordinary limit
checks.reason: For fixed K,tau, b_delta,J->0 removes the b^nu and delta log2 terms. epsilon_J->0 at fixed eta then removes the residual term. tau->0 at fixed K removes (2qC_K/B)tau even if C_K grows rapidly. K->infinity uses K-independent c_B and r>nu. R>=1 gives the lower bound, so both outer liminf and limsup are 0. No C(J)epsilon_J inference, joint limit or exchange appears.

checks.claim: Section 7 Q_J H_W measurability through transferred Lp limits and completions; independence of the finite raw head only
checks.reason: Coefficients W(Q_J T f_k) are orthogonal to W(e_j) and jointly Gaussian. Lp limits are measurable for the completed field via an a.s. subsequence. A pi-system argument gives independence of the tuple from the finite vector G. Time blocks remain correlated and no block independence is used.

checks.claim: Finite-dimensional product-law freezing (21), conditional inequality (7) and J=0
checks.reason: f is Borel on R^J x B0^n because g->Phi(g) is continuous. psi is Borel by Tonelli. The product law gives E[f(G,X)|G]=psi(G) in the extended nonnegative sense. psi(g)<=R_delta,J on ||Phi(g)||<=M by definition, and a single Borel version avoids an uncountable null intersection. J=0 gives Phi=0, which lies in the ball since M>0, so the claim holds unconditionally.

checks.claim: Global physical product (22) only a norm majorant
checks.reason: Submultiplicativity plus z<=max(1,z) gives (22). The note explicitly disclaims a global restart identity, sharp deterministic growth, the tail ||Phi_delta,J||>M and M->infinity.

checks.claim: Exact upstream fit of objects and parameters (all Gamma, d=1,2,3, fixed R, B, delta, r, p, theta, F, T, P_J, X_m, Y, b, g_delta)
checks.reason: Ranges, intervals, stopped extensions, the norm Y, C0, epsilon_J, A_nu and first-J convention agree line by line with C3 Sections 1,4,7-8 and D1 Section 1. This was a fit check, and the upstream notes were not recertified.

minor: Optional clarity, lines 211-213: the step identifying the head coefficient leaves two facts implicit. They are (a) the head transfer is a finite combination with deterministic path coefficients, for example by rank-one transfer or the first-chaos identity ell(X^0-X^J)=W(P_J k_ell), and (b) E[X_m W(e_j)]=0. Both follow directly from accepted inputs, so this is not a gap.

Optional clarity, lines 202-204: (14) contains no J and holds for arbitrary Phi, so the remark that it is uniform in J because ||P_J Phi||<=||Phi|| is stray. Phi_delta,J is not P_J of a bounded H vector. Boundedness comes only from the cutoff ||Phi_delta,J||<=M.

Optional clarity, lines 231-232: the baseline computation evaluates only the displacement column, with velocity entry 0 and tau(ell)(1,0)=(1,0). The phrase saying it uses BOTH constant columns overstates that step, although both columns are present in F and in H_m.
Optional clarity, lines 276-283: joint Borel measurability on the product relies on separability of H and B0^n, which is supplied upstream but not restated here.

Optional clarity: statement note 2 asked for symbols to be disambiguated, but overloads remain and rely on context. R is the fixed radius, the inverse path and R_delta,J. G is the linear map, the Gaussian head and G_B. P is P_J, P_m and UV. Q is the local evolution and Q_J. H is the driver and the Hilbert space. K is the constant and K(F). C_B and c_B are near-identical names for distinct constants. No formula is ambiguous in context.

Optional clarity: line 71 lists C_K as depending on theta,B,K, while c_B is said to depend also on the fixed free group. Since C_K>=c_B, it inherits G_B. G_B is determined by B for this fixed S_F, so this is harmless.

limitations: This is a read-only AI review, not human verification, a novelty audit, a full-goal certificate or a Lean formalization. The E1-E4 arguments remain informal analytic proofs.
Upstream accepted notes (fixed-mask, C3, D1, source-operator Theorem 1) were read completely and checked for exact fit. They were not broadly recertified, and the result is conditional on them.

Primary source coverage is the three selected page images and the selected excerpt only, not a full-book audit. Dimension-free validity rests on the book's statement that C depends on alpha+beta and on Section 1.5.

The reviewer did no script execution or hashing. Image and text SHA values, Git revisions such as cf0cf05 and d2f9a9c, and the 73 facts/19 seams and timing provenance figures were not independently verified. JSON controls were checked by reading the script and by hand recomputation of selected rows.
The Mathlib application was checked against the frozen printed type only. No compiler or kernel was run by the reviewer.
